restatements.text: Requires individuals who keep firearms in a residence to store them in a locked container when not being carried or used.
Requires the Department to issue storage certificates to applicants who pay a $25 fee.
Preempts local governments from adopting or enforcing firearm storage ordinances, making the state the sole authority on the matter.

analysis.answer: Currently, there is no state law governing residential firearm storage. This clause establishes a statewide mandate requiring individuals to store firearms in locked containers when not carried or used.
Firearm owners will incur the direct cost of purchasing locked containers, such as safes or lockboxes, if they do not already possess them.
Firearm owners without secure storage will likely purchase lockboxes or safes to comply with the mandate.

The clause addresses the risk of unauthorized access to firearms in the home (e.g., by children or thieves). The mechanism reaches this by explicitly mandating locked storage when firearms are not actively in use.
Applicants will face a direct cost of $25 per certificate. The state will incur administrative costs to process applications and issue the certificates.
Those applying for the certificate pay the $25 fee. The state department receives the revenue to fund the administration of the certificate program.

The text creates a storage certificate and sets an application fee, but does not provide a mechanism linking the certificate to any requirement, creating an information gap regarding who must apply or what the certificate accomplishes.

Currently, cities and counties may adopt their own ordinances regarding firearm storage. This clause preempts local governments from doing so, granting exclusive regulatory authority over the matter to the state.
The state government gains exclusive regulatory power over firearm storage, while city and county governments lose their discretion to set or enforce local storage standards.

flags.note: The text mandates an agency to issue certificates but does not define or identify which state department it refers to.
